statement: Let sigma be the normalized projector onto the fresh-public Johnston-Lovitz 4x4 symmetric/Dicke support L=D H D, D=diag(1,sqrt3,sqrt3,1), H the 4x4 Hankel subspace. For every positive semidefinite 4x4 bipartite operator tau, there exists epsilon_0(tau)>0 such that sigma+epsilon*tau has Schmidt number at most 2 for all 0<=epsilon<epsilon_0. In particular, for any pure vector v the conclusion holds for sufficiently small epsilon in sigma+epsilon[v], without requiring PPT. The threshold is existential, depends on tau, and no claim is made for the entire PPT interval or other base states. This is a WRITTEN candidate requiring independent review.
provenance_and_imports: The base is explicitly the public arXiv:2609.11849v1 sections 1.2, 2.1, 2.3, read under the later frontier-first source ruling; no stopped historical audit, selected-parameter episode or held consumer is used. The all-vector range result frontier-20261028-hankel-one-vector-range-v1.json SHA256 f9d7a7beeb70612e8a2698e962cbe04b9549ff9e644a33c1a50b4dfd0035bc0e is used as an unreviewed lemma for existence of an exterior rank-two point, with its algebraic-geometry imports. Additional named imports are the projective dimension theorem, the standard secant parametrization by unordered pairs of points of P1, Chevalley's constructible-image theorem, and finite-dimensional convex separation/interior. No formal or independent review or novelty claim.
base_is_relative_interior: The coherent product kets h(z) are normalized local tensor squares of (1,sqrt3*z,sqrt3*z^2,z^3)/(1+|z|^2)^(3/2), including z=infinity. Their projectors integrate to sigma with the full-support normalized Fubini-Study measure: angular integration enforces equal anti-diagonal index n, and the radial beta integral gives n!(6-n)!/7!=1/(7*binomial(6,n)). Thus sigma is in the relative interior of the closed cone C generated by these product projectors in its real linear span: a supporting functional vanishing on the full-support average vanishes on every generator. Choose seven distinct coherent kets h_i spanning L. Consequently sigma-epsilon*sum_i[h_i] is separable for all sufficiently small epsilon>0. Each sum [h_i]+[h_j] is (1/4) times the sum of [h_i+alpha*h_j] over alpha=1,-1,i,-i. These 84 Schmidt-rank<=2 projectors span Herm(L), because their sums recover the seven [h_i] and their differences recover all real and imaginary cross terms. Therefore epsilon*sum_i[h_i] is an interior point of the Schmidt-number<=2 cone on Herm(L); adding the separable residual shows sigma itself is interior in that cone.
outside_component_span: Fix V outside H and E=span(H,V). The predecessor proves that X={rank<=2} in P^15 has an exterior point in P(E), so some irreducible component R of X intersect P(E) is not contained in P(H). We claim R can be chosen with projective linear span P(E). If V is symmetric, use instead the symmetric rank<=2 variety Y in P^9: each component R of Y intersect P(E) has dimension at least 4; R intersect P(H) has dimension at least 3 and lies in the irreducible threefold Z=X intersect P(H), hence contains Z. Since Z contains and spans the rational normal sextic, R spans P(E). For nonsymmetric V, any component R not contained in P(H) has dimension at least 3. If dim R>=4, its hyperplane section inside P(H) has dimension at least 3, so it contains Z and again spans P(E). Suppose dim R=3. Then R intersect P(H) has dimension 2; its generic point is rank two. At such a point the predecessor's tangent computation implies that any intersection with another component is possible only when k1^T(V-V^T)k2=0. The unordered pair of roots of the rank-two Hankel recurrence defines a point in Sym^2(P1)=P2, and this tangent equation is a nonzero homogeneous quadratic in its coordinates. Its inverse image in Z is a union of irreducible secant-line surfaces, one for each irreducible component of that conic; the dimension-2 set R intersect P(H) contains one such surface. Every projective curve in the pair plane meets every pencil of pairs containing a fixed point of P1. Thus that surface contains, in closure, every point of the rational normal sextic and spans P(H). Therefore R contains a spanning subset of P(H) and also a point outside P(H), so spans P(E). The nonzero quadratic and transversality calculations are those explicitly stated in the predecessor; equality at double roots is interpreted via the tangent secant limit.
complex_affine_convexity: On such an irreducible R, take the affine chart of E with coefficient of V equal to 1 and write its points V+h with h in H. Their affine hull is all of H, since R spans P(E). Every nonzero complex-linear functional on H is nonconstant on this irreducible affine variety; by constructibility its image in C is cofinite. Hence the real part of every nonzero complex-linear functional is unbounded above and below there. Every real-linear functional is of this form, so finite-dimensional separation gives the whole real H as the closure of the convex hull; because the convex hull is convex and has full-dimensional closure, it equals H. In particular there are finitely many rank<=2 V+h_j and positive weights p_j summing to 1 with sum_j p_j*h_j=0.
pure_and_mixed_conclusion: The cancellation identity sum_j p_j[V+h_j]=[V]+sum_j p_j[h_j] holds exactly. Since sigma is interior in the Schmidt-number<=2 cone on L, sigma-epsilon*sum_j p_j[h_j] has Schmidt number<=2 for sufficiently small epsilon. The identity then gives sigma+epsilon[V] as a sum of that residual and rank<=2 projectors. Local invertible maps carry the Hankel proof to L=DHD without changing ranks. For an arbitrary positive tau=sum_(j=1)^m[v_j], choose epsilon small enough that all m states sigma+m*epsilon[v_j] have Schmidt number<=2; their average is sigma+epsilon*tau. No uniform epsilon across all tau, PPT-interval upper bound, or Schmidt-number-three target claim follows.
